study_identification_part.si4_title: Brain morphology normative modelling platform for abnormality and centile estimation: Brain MoNoCle

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Present Brain MoNoCle, an open-source web platform with pre-trained normative models for cortical morphology that estimates individual abnormalities (z-scores, centiles) and supports group/individual analyses, and validate it on bipolar disorder and temporal lobe epilepsy cohorts.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: TLE: regional abnormalities (Cohen's d) correlated with ENIGMA effect sizes (r>0.5) and lateralisation predicted from hemisphere z-score differences (accuracy 0.782). BD: group outputs aligned with literature only after normative modelling; cross-app validation showed good agreement of z-scores with CentileBrain.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Pre-trained GAMLSS-based normative models on 3,276 HCs across 21 sites enable robust individual z/centile scoring; validations show agreement with prior large consortia, accurate TLE lateralisation, and highlight superior age/sex modeling for the K morphometric.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Normative models trained on 3,276 HCs from 21 sites (age 5–95) using GAMLSS (shash) with sex fixed effects, site random effects, and smooth age captured mean/variance/skew/kurtosis. QC combined statistical outlier detection (>5 MAD residuals) and visual checks with listwise deletion. Stability analyses with 200 held-out subjects showed residual correlations >0.995 and MAE convergence ~n=2000. Different-domain validations: regional cortical thickness effects in IDEAS TLE agreed with ENIGMA (r>0.5), hemisphere z-score differences predicted lateralisation with accuracy 0.782 (best for cortical volume), and z-scores correlated well with CentileBrain. Among metrics, the independent morphometric K achieved R2≈0.8 versus 0.4–0.6 for traditional measures, suggesting improved nuisance modeling and sensitivity.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Open web R Shiny app integrates with FreeSurfer outputs; supports group and individual outputs (z, centiles), hemisphere and 68 ROI analyses; model-based site harmonisation (random effects + local HC calibration); includes traditional and independent morphometrics (K, I, S).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Current platform focuses on cortical measures (e.g., limited detection of subcortical abnormalities in mTLE); FreeSurfer versions vary across datasets (handled via harmonisation); requires local HCs for calibration of new sites and SD estimation (if <30 HCs, uses normative SD proxy).

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Platform URL: https://cnnplab.shinyapps.io/BrainMoNoCle/ . Normative datasets listed in Supp S1 include ADHD1000, CamCAN, HCP, NKI, OASIS3, MEGUK sites, NCL-dementia, NIMH-IHV, Stanford-CR, UCLH, Chronotype, Greene-HM, BLISS. Age range 5–95. Preprocessing via FreeSurfer recon-all + localGI; 68 DK regions. Modeling: GAMLSS (shash) with sex fixed, site random, smooth(age) for mean/sd, skew~sex+smooth(age), kurtosis~smooth(age). New-site calibration uses local HCs to compute offsets and SD (if <30 HCs use normative average SD). Future roadmap mentions multiscale morphometrics, additional atlases, vertex-wise, longitudinal extensions.
